relations.subject: sgw:role
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - Capella's requiresCapellaRole and server's requiresPrivilege both gate an operation behind a fixed enum; here a role is itself defined as a bundle of channel grants, so the relation runs role -> channel, not operation -> role
relations.evidence: A Role and a user assigned to a role is granted to access to a channel, which is associated with a specific collection.

relations.subject: sgw:user
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - closest promoted relation (groupMembersInheritRole) describes a group inheriting a role; here the inheritance is of channel access via role membership, a different object type, so a new predicate was minted
relations.evidence: Any user associated with a role inherits the right to access any of the channels in the role's list.

relations.subject: sgw:role
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - no prior relation captures two entity kinds sharing a namespace-collision-free space
relations.evidence: Roles have a separate namespace from users, so it's possible to have a user and a role with the same name.

relations.subject: sgw:role
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - revokesRole (promoted) is about removing a role grant from a user; this is about deleting the role entity itself cascading to loss of channel access for all its members
relations.evidence: removing a role effectively revokes access to the channel that role is associated with and may mean users will lose access to required documents.

relations.subject: sgw:role
relations.evidence: Roles are created via the Sync Gateway Admin REST API — see: [Admin REST API](../rest-api/rest-api-admin.md).

cross_product_finding: Roles here are not a fixed, product-defined enum (unlike server/'s named RBAC privileges or Capella's catalog of management-plane roles) - they are arbitrary, admin-created bundles of channel grants, scoped per scope/collection. The 'role grants channel access, user inherits via role membership' shape has no counterpart in either prior batch: server/ and Capella both gate *operations* behind a role/privilege, whereas SGW roles are themselves containers of *data-access* grants. Also notable: SGW explicitly allows a role and a user to share the same name (separate namespaces) - a modeling choice neither server/ RBAC nor Capella's IAM-style roles exhibit as far as covered.
